By mtime the order is v2 (03:02:05, pinning the pre-v3 parent 11a305c6), then core-gate-harness-specifications.v3 (03:08:08), then this v1 (03:13:09, pinning v3), then v3 (07:39:03, also pinning v3). So v1 is not an obsolete first draft - it is the file authored once the accepted parent existed, and it is the only one of the three sitting at the D-086 promised path. v2's own authorityClaim is candid about this, saying the path is 'occupied at v2' rather than claiming the promised path.

CROSS-ARTIFACT NOTE ON v3, raised without reopening it. harness.DR-G02.core-installed.v3, which I accepted earlier in this session at f4a68e0d, carries an authorityClaim stating 'This file exists so the D-086 promised artifactPathWhenAuthored is occupied against the accepted parent' while itself sitting at .v3.json. The promised path is .v1.json and is occupied by this subject. v2's wording was more precise about the same point. That v3 dispatch's attack list did not include the path question, which is why it did not surface then; I record it now because reviewing v1 is what made the structure legible. Whether v3's wording needs tightening, or whether three files at three paths for one promised occupancy is itself worth consolidating, is the coordinator's call, not a defect in this subject.

Live gate-harness-naming.v6 records DR-G02 artifactExists false, while this file exists at exactly the artifactPathWhenAuthored that same entry names. That drift is now directly material rather than incidental, because occupancy of that path is this file's entire purpose. Correcting it is an MF-6 register-content change requiring a decision, not an act of this specification. I have recorded the same drift at DR-G07, DR-G16, DR-G19 and DR-G22 this session.

This file's authorityClaim omits the explicit denials v3 carries - does not SATISFY DR-101, does not close OBL-2, does not invent a D-006 unit, does not authorize implementation. Not charged: silence is not a claim, OBL-2 and required-now occur zero times so neither can be asserted or changed, and status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with binds NOTHING carries the standing. v3's wording is nonetheless stronger on this point.

The 83886080 refusal is the substantive merit of this specification and it is identical in v1 and v3 - the harness objects are byte-identical. The constant is 80 MiB in bytes, the conversion D-006 has never authorized; naming it only to refuse it, and deferring the size comparison to a unit-and-accounting successor, keeps a product question from being settled by arithmetic.
